issue_context.title: Feature Request: Search
issue_context.body:
One of the superior features of iTerm2 (sadly only available on macOS) is it's content search.  The search comes in two variants: search from active tab and search from all tabs. For those unfamiliar with iTerm2 and wondering, this feature would roughly equate to almost any editor like Visual Studio Code string search.

I haven't gone in-depth with the output buffering in Terminal yet to validate if this feature is realistically doable at the current state of the Terminal app, but this is a usability feature for multitasking terminal users that would be worth a LOT.
comments: I'll repurpose this as our main Search epic issue. I'm glad the community seems to have figured out our backlog and I don't need to go add it myself. :smile:

That would be pretty great 👀 
With regex support ? 😸

Another thing to keep in consideration about how iTerm2 works, is you can "Ctrl+f" to search, then press Tab when you find what you want, and it will copy what you searched for.  Basically you can easily find something in the output and copy/paste it to the input without ever leaving your keyboard.

It will be great if the search history can be traversed with `Arrow up` and `Arrow down` key.

BTW just a suggestion. 😸
(for the record, I believe #3279 was the first step on the path to this feature landing, but it's not quite finished yet. Thanks though msftbot)
Amazing! Can we expect a new search feature in the next release?

@kell18 While this feature is in active development currently, I _personally_ don't think it's going to make it quite in time for the next release cut unfortunately. Ideally, it _should_ land in the December release (which is why this is marked for the "1912" milestone), but I'm making no commitments 😝

:tada:This issue was addressed in #3590, which has now been successfully released as `Windows Terminal Preview v0.8.10091.0`.:tada:

review_comments: We had an offline discussion on `ColorSelection()`. This is a feature we don't want because it would overwrite some contents of the text buffer. So (for now at least) don't do anything that modifies the contents of the buffer. Only the selection.

If ConHost and Windows Terminal differ here, why not make a cleaner separation between their implementations? We could make `Search` an abstract class. Then implement it in ConHost with the color feature, and implement it in Windows Terminal without. That way, we don't have these functions that we're using completely differently.

Would that be overkill though? I'd like to hear thoughts from the team on this topic too.

Shouldn't this be a Windows Terminal specific implementation? If we wanted, conhost could have it and then make or modify an existing API in ConPTY or Conhost so other terminals could make use of the feature. If that is the case, then we would inherit the functionality, not duplicate the implementation. I think having Windows Terminal specific is probably the best route for us though. Other terminals could still implement this if they wanted.
@DHowett @miniksa I would prefer to keep the current design here. ColorSelection is the only method that differs, so I think it is not necessary to make big changes here.

I don't really like that `Color` doesn't do what it says it does when projected into the `Terminal`, but I'm concerned that might be too many moving pieces all at once here. Perhaps we should file a follow-on work item to decide what to actually to with the color selection. I could see it being useful in the Terminal, though perhaps it shouldn't actually modify the text buffer state. To be fair, maybe it shouldn't be modifying the real text buffer state in Conhost either and we should just fix the impl overall.
Thanks for the suggestion, I also think we should have a follow-on work for this issue. This requires more design and bigger change, so I think it is not good to let this refactor block Search.
I created a new issue for this: https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/3542
I am OK taking it as a future work item. Thank you, Kaiyu.
Just attach the work item Michael was talking about here and I'll approve it.
